title: New Cinderella Movie 'Steps' Gets a Famous Composer
summary:
Have you ever wondered what happened to Cinderella's evil stepsisters after the ball? Well, Netflix has a new movie about them! It's called 'Steps,' and it's coming out on November 20. And guess what? The music is being composed by Kris Bowers, a super talented guy who's been nominated for an Emmy.

Kris recorded the score at the famous Abbey Road Studios in London — the same place where The Beatles made their music! He said he wanted the music to make you remember the whole movie just by listening to it.

The movie is about Lilith, one of the stepsisters, who gets blamed for stealing a magic wand and crashing the Royal Ball. She accidentally turns her sister Margot into a frog! Now she has to team up with Cinderella (yes, the real Cinderella!) and a dreamy troll to save the kingdom and prove that even 'villains' deserve a happy ending.

The voice cast is amazing: Ali Wong plays Lilith, Stephanie Hsu is Margot, Amanda Seyfried is Cinderella, Bette Midler is the fairy godmother, Daniel Radcliffe (Harry Potter!) plays a royal, and Peter Dinklage is 'The Muscle.'

The directors, Alyce Tzue and John Ripa, said Kris is a dream to work with. Alyce said, 'When he plays piano, it's like he draws a string from what he's feeling through the instrument to his audience.' That's so cool!

Alyce also said the story is personal to her because she grew up feeling like an outsider. She wanted to make a film for everyone who ever felt like they didn't belong. So this movie is about kindness and finding your place. I can't wait to see it!
why_it_matters: The movie reminds you that everyone, even people who make big mistakes or feel left out, can be the hero of their own story if they choose kindness.

background_read: Abbey Road Studios is a world-famous recording studio in London where The Beatles (one of the most popular rock bands in history) made many of their classic songs.
The story of Cinderella has been retold in many movies, but this is one of the first to make the stepsisters the main characters, showing that 'villains' can have complex stories too.
Article_Structure: WHO: Voice actors Ali Wong (Lilith), Stephanie Hsu (Margot), Amanda Seyfried (Cinderella), Bette Midler (fairy godmother), Daniel Radcliffe, Peter Dinklage, and composer Kris Bowers.
WHAT: A new animated film 'Steps' where a stepsister accidentally turns her sister into a frog and must team up with Cinderella and a troll to save the kingdom.
WHERE: The music was recorded at the historic Abbey Road Studios, and the film will be released on Netflix on November 20.
WHY: To share a message of kindness, show that even people called villains deserve redemption, and make a film for anyone who has felt like an outsider.

perspectives.description: They see this as a chance to flip a famous fairy tale and prove that everyone's side of the story matters, especially those who are often misjudged.
Some people might find it strange to make the 'evil' stepsisters into main heroes, because they are used to the classic good-vs-evil version.
For children who have ever felt like outsiders at school or in a friend group, this movie sends a comforting message that they belong and can be brave helpers.
